thread:
jamie: Heads up — eu-central1 pod pool 'gpu-4' showing sustained NVMe write util ~95%. GPU attach times up ~18-25s. Graphs line up with metadata repair/anti-entropy runs.
ana: Ugh, saw a bunch of unattached VMs in the prov queue this morning. Any clue which process is generating that write churn?
mike: quick check: control-plane logs show repeated raft repair jobs kicking off after leader flips. Looks like the repair loop rewrites tombstones aggressively. snippet from meta-repair.log:\n```
2026-03-21T07:12:10Z repair_worker.go: rewrite_tombstones=12467 bytes_written=1.2G duration=4.1s
2026-03-21T07:12:15Z repair_worker.go: rewrite_tombstones=13210 bytes_written=1.4G duration=4.6s
```
lia: That write pattern would definitely spike small-random writes. NVMe is getting write amplification + GC pressure. Any correlation with our janitor/compact jobs?
jamie: Janitor runs at 03:00 UTC, this is around 07:10 UTC. Different schedule. Looks like anti-entropy is on a 5m cadence after leader changes. We had a flurry of elections in eu-central earlier.
ops-bot: :warning: Alert: eu-central1 nvme_write_iops > 80k for 12m (sustained). Impact: provisioning delays and 4 attach errors. Incident created: INF-4235
ana: Can we throttle the repair job or add a rate limiter asap?
mike: I can push a quick flag change to pause repair writes to below 100MB/s per worker. Will need a short restart of the repair controller (stateless). Lia, can you validate this won't break quorum?
lia: Pausing aggressive repair is ok for a short window; anti-entropy can lag a bit. But do NOT disable KV tombstone compaction entirely. We should also pin the raft leaders to reduce churn.
jamie: Action plan: 1) mike -> deploy repair rate limiter (10x throttle) now. 2) ana -> pin leaders for hot partitions in eu-central (manual allocation) 3) lia -> add safety doc on safe repair backoff. 4) ops-bot -> notify Dedicated to scale ephemeral pool if attach delays persist.
ana: I'll start leader pin after mike deploys. Also scheduling a maintenance window 09:00 UTC to run a controlled compaction at low concurrency.
mike: Deploying limiter now. Command I ran: `kubectl set env deployment/repair-controller REPAIR_WRITE_LIMIT=100MB_S` and restarted pods. Watching IOPS.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Repair-controller rollout started. New pods becoming ready.
jamie: Early telemetry: write_iops dropped ~65% within 90s, attach latency back to normal for a few test jobs. Keeping open to watch for 30m.
lia: Filing follow-up RFC to change repair strategy — avoid full tombstone rewrites during leader flaps, add exponential backoff + leader-stable window.
ana: Filed INF-4235 with notes and linked RFC D-1278. Assigning owners.
jamie: Thanks team. If I see any attach errors again I'll @oncall.
